info.cls_ename: Department of Foreign Languages and Literature

description.describe_ch: 本課程旨在教導學生基本英文寫作之過程及技巧，主題包括預寫技巧，寫作步驟，文章修改與編輯及同儕互評。寫作練習以不同修辭文體之段落寫作及句構練習為主。課程結合主題式文體分析與寫作實踐。透過寫作練習，同學將學習文章撰寫、編輯與修訂的技巧。與課同學將於學期末彙整完成的稿件，以作品集呈現。
description.describe_eh: This course equips students with basic writing skills such as prewriting techniques, steps in writing, and bases for revision and editing. Students’ assignments cover paragraph/essay writing in different rhetorical modes, and English sentence skill practices. Students will present a final portfolio displaying the outcomes of their writing drafts.

gradeRuleDescribe.tpa_score_new:
Students’ final grades will be determined by five key components of their academic performance: attendance, participation, drafts, and exams. Further descriptions of each category are as follows:
 
Attendance (0%)
Attendance is mandatory. The instructor will take attendance at the beginning of each class from September 17th to December 31st. It is the students’ responsibility to sign in for their attendance; otherwise, they may be marked as absent.
Each student is allowed up to 3 unpenalized absences during the semester. Additional absences beyond these may be excused under the following conditions:
 
(i) If a student must miss one or more classes for a legitimate reason, such as attending a conference, a competition, or an interview, the absence(s) can be excused provided the student submits an official document verifying the reason either in advance or afterward.
(ii) If a student misses one or more classes due to an emergency or unanticipated event, the absence(s) can be excused provided the student submits an official document verifying the occurrence afterward.
Excluding the additional absences that can be excused under the conditions stated above, students will receive a 2-point deduction from their final overall score for each unexcused absence from the 4th to the 5th, in addition to the initial 3 unpenalized absences. If a student accumulates 6 or more unexcused absences overall, they will fail the course automatically. Furthermore, if a student has 6 or more absences overall, including the initial 3 unpenalized absences, regardless of their legitimacy, the student’s final course grade will be the original grade lowered by two letters (e.g. A+ → A- ; B+ → B- ; C+ → C- ; and so on.).
Students will be marked as absent even if they are present under the following conditions:
(i)  They arrive to class more than 10 minutes late without a legitimate reason.
(ii) They leave the class early without obtaining the instructor’s permission before the start of the class.
(iii) They become distracted in class by engaging in other activities, such as using their mobile devices (especially their cellphones!), chatting, sleeping, doing homework, or preparing for a quiz or an exam for the next class, etc.
Students with perfect attendance (no absence, lateness, or tardiness) will be awarded with a 2-point bonus added to theirfinal overall score.
  • Grading Scale
A+   90–100     A   85–89     A-   80–84
B+   77–79       B   73–76      B-   70–72
C+   67–69       C   63–66      C-   60–62
D     40–59
E     1–39
X     0
  • See FCU Grading Scale at:
https://myfcu.fcu.edu.tw/main/S6800/S680004_Out_Download.aspx?originfilename=(%E5%85%AC%E5%91%8A)%E9%80%A2%E7%94%B2%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%B8%E5%AD%B8%E7%94%9F%E5%AD%B8%E6%A5%AD%E6%88%90%E7%B8%BE%E8%A9%95%E9%87%8F%E8%A6%81%E9%BB%9E_%E4%BF%AE%E8%A8%82%E5%85%A8%E6%96%87_1130329.pdf&newfilename=4c20cf706cf749e8963448d426a337ac_2_1.pdf.
 
Participation (10%)
Students are encouraged to speak up, ask questions, and actively participate in group discussions and in-class activities. Nevertheless, tardiness and in-class disruptions, such as sleeping in class, using cellphones, or any behaviors that interrupt class, will negatively impact their participation grade.
 
The Practice of Proper Writing Process, Self-evaluation, and Peer Review (25%)
In addition to their drafts, students will be evaluated on how effectively they practice the writing process (brainstorming, exploring, organizing, (re)writing, and editing) and how they assess their own work based on feedback from the instructor and peers. Groups of 4 to 5 students will collaborate by reviewing one another’s work to support their peers in becoming better writers in this course.
 
Drafts (45%)
Students will submit at least 3 drafts for 3 topics this semester, with each draft contributing 5% to their final grade. When working on their drafts, students are required to use the writing process worksheet to document their writing process and to evaluate their writing using the self-evaluation chart afterward. Both documents can be found on iLearn. Further details on writing each draft for a topic are provided below:
(i)  Before writing their first drafts for a topic, students are required to complete the two stages of writing process (Explore and Organize) on the writing process worksheet to familiarize themselves with the topic they are working on. Once they have a better understanding of the topic, students can begin to write their first drafts on it and submit their works in class on the due date.
(ii) Students can expect to receive their first drafts, reviewed by the instructor, in the following week. Once they have it, they will discuss their first drafts with peers, providing mutual feedback to one another’s works. They will evaluate their works using the self-evaluation chart, documenting the issues identified in their first drafts. Subsequently, students will write their second drafts based on the feedback from the instructor and their peers.
(iii) Student will bring their writing process worksheets, self-evaluation charts, and second drafts to class the following week. In the class of that week, they will review the issues they encountered in their first drafts, how they addressed these issues in their second drafts, and the reasoning behind their chosen solutions. At the end of the class, they will submit their second drafts to the instructor. Students will repeat steps (ii) and (iii) while writing, revising, and editing an essay on a given topic as they work on their third and subsequent drafts.
All drafts are due in class as hard copies. Late submissions will not be accepted and will receive a grade of zero. Students who have 3 and more late submissions will automatically fail the cou
